title_en: White House event reveals Ukraine and Russia share one goal: flattering Melania
title_zh: 白宫活动显示乌克兰和俄罗斯有一个共同目标：奉承梅拉尼娅

summary_zh: 随着基辅和其他城市的战争愈演愈烈，第一夫人在讲台上与俄罗斯和乌克兰特使庆祝单城停火
body_en: As war rages on in Kyiv and other cities, the first lady celebrates her single-city ceasefire with Russian and Ukrainian envoys

B eaming from a podium in the White House’s Grand Foyer, Melania Trump welcomed senior Russian and Ukrainian officials on Thursday to celebrate a ceasefire in an embattled Ukrainian town for which she has become the unlikeliest broker.

The evacuation from Oleshky, a frontline Ukrainian town now occupied by Russia where 800 people lived through a protracted humanitarian crisis, may seem like a sideshow at this point in the war. Russian missiles and drones continue to rain down on Kyiv and other major cities, and a single Russian strike described as a “double-tap” bombing killed 40 people in Zaporizhzhia on Wednesday.

So it could have been easy to brush the White House meeting off as a chance for Ukraine and Russia to flatter the first lady. And flatter her they did, praising her for her diplomatic acumen, delivering her state awards and even gifting her trinkets of thanks from the residents of Oleshky whom she saved. In case the subtext was not yet clear, a children’s drawing gifted by the Russian side was inscribed: “I love Melania.”

But there was real diplomatic juice in the room as Trump, a former model who has occupied a relatively quiet role in her husband’s second term as president, now played host to one of the highest-level gatherings of Russian and Ukrainian officials in recent months.

Kirill Dmitriev, the sanctioned head of the Russian Direct Investment Fund who regularly negotiates for Moscow, was seated next to Davyd Arakhamia, the head of Volodymyr Zelenskyy’s Servant of the People party and a chief negotiator for Ukraine. Next to them were Ukraine’s Dmytro Lubinets and Russia’s Yana Lantratova, the respective human rights ombudspeople who have become an unlikely and respectful double act throughout the evacuation process.

The meeting came after a particularly bitter public feud between Zelenskyy and Trump, as the US cut intelligence sharing and satellite internet in recent weeks in an apparent effort to pressure Kyiv into capitulating. And the Trump administration’s plans with Russia are in peril after the midterms, with triumphant Democrats promising to investigate senior aides to Trump who had pitched Russia on business deals to end the war in Ukraine.

But everyone at the White House on Thursday was focused on feting Melania, whose role in brokering the ceasefire was extensively praised at every opportunity – even if her descriptions of reviewing de-mining plans and assessing evacuation routes strained belief.

As well as the drawing, Dmitriev extended her a personal expression of gratitude from Vladimir Putin, while on the Ukrainian side, Lubinets presented her with the order of Princess Olga, first class – one of the country’s highest honours. He also issued a general request: “Please continue to do your wonderful work and support people.”
Stepping into the role of diplomat and humanitarian, the first lady called for “humanity over war” and said that she hoped the limited ceasefire in the frontline town would “inspire greater peace”.

“Together, we can create something more enduring than a temporary ceasefire,” she said. “Let us see Oleshky as a spark in a world of darkness, capable of illuminating the best in humanity. Build a powerful flame of peace, visible to the world. Ignite hope, foster cooperation and brighten a path toward lasting peace.”
Later, she handed personal letters to Dmitriev and Arakhamia to bring back to Putin and Zelenskyy.

Donald Trump didn’t attend, and didn’t have any public events on his schedule on Tuesday. Later in the day, he said he met with Dimitriev but not with Ukrainian officials, and refused to say what they discussed. The president’s absence from the White House event was conspicuous, both because of the high-profile guests, and because of his own well-known interest in being seen as a peacemaker. While he has publicly demanded the Nobel peace prize, on Thursday it was Melania who was being crowned the humanitarian-in-chief.

It was an unusual role for her. She has not taken part in high-level negotiations between Ukraine and Russia before, and is said behind the scenes to have been critical of her husband’s heavy-handed approach to dealing with Ukraine.
But she has increasingly engaged in humanitarian efforts related to the conflict, first by working on a program that reunified more than 30 children displaced from their families during the conflict.

In Oleshky, she also claimed to have been involved in “every stage” of the planning. To do so, she said, she had “reviewed de-mining plans, aerial images, assessed roadways, and discussed evacuation routes, hospital access, vehicles and medical resources”.
Now the White House has cast her as a dark horse diplomat.

“This unprecedented gathering marks the first time in US history that an American first lady has personally brought representatives of two nations actively at war together at the White House to pursue diplomatic and humanitarian objectives,” said Marc Beckman, an aide who is self-described as her exclusive senior adviser.
What’s clear is that at this moment both sides have recognised the need to keep Melania – and the testy Trump administration – onside.
body_zh: 随着基辅和其他城市的战争愈演愈烈，第一夫人与俄罗斯和乌克兰特使庆祝单城停火
周四，梅拉尼娅·特朗普在白宫大厅的讲台上满面笑容地欢迎俄罗斯和乌克兰高级官员，庆祝陷入困境的乌克兰小镇实现停火，而她已成为最不可能的掮客。
奥列什基是乌克兰前线城镇，现已被俄罗斯占领，那里有 800 人正在经历一场旷日持久的人道主义危机，从奥列什基的撤离在战争的这个阶段似乎只是一场余兴节目。俄罗斯导弹和无人机继续袭击基辅和其他主要城市，周三，俄罗斯一次被称为“双击”轰炸的袭击在扎波罗热造成 40 人死亡。
因此，很容易将白宫会议视为乌克兰和俄罗斯奉承第一夫人的机会。他们还奉承她，赞扬她的外交头脑，授予她国家奖项，甚至还赠送了她拯救的奥列什基居民的感谢礼物。如果潜台词还不清楚的话，俄罗斯方面赠送的一幅儿童画上写着：“我爱梅拉尼娅。”
但房间里确实充满了外交活力，因为特朗普曾是一名模特，在丈夫的第二个总统任期内扮演着相对安静的角色，现在主持了近几个月来俄罗斯和乌克兰官员最高级别的聚会之一。
经常为莫斯科进行谈判的俄罗斯直接投资基金负责人基里尔·德米特里耶夫坐在弗拉基米尔·泽连斯基的人民公仆党主席、乌克兰首席谈判代表达维德·阿拉卡米亚旁边。他们旁边是乌克兰的德米特罗·鲁宾涅茨（Dmytro Lubinets）和俄罗斯的亚娜·兰特拉托娃（Yana Lantratova），他们分别是人权监察员，在整个撤离过程中，他们成为了令人难以置信且令人尊敬的双重角色。
这次会议是在泽伦斯基和特朗普之间发生特别激烈的公开争执之后举行的，美国最近几周削减了情报共享和卫星互联网，显然是为了迫使基辅投降。特朗普政府与俄罗斯的计划在中期选举后面临危险，胜利的民主党人承诺调查特朗普的高级助手，这些助手曾向俄罗斯推销结束乌克兰战争的商业协议。
但周四，白宫的每个人都把注意力集中在庆祝梅拉尼娅身上，她在斡旋停火方面的作用一有机会就受到广泛赞扬——尽管她对审查排雷计划和评估疏散路线的描述令人难以置信。
除了绘画之外，德米特里耶夫还向她表达了弗拉基米尔·普京个人的谢意，而在乌克兰方面，卢宾涅茨则向她颁发了奥尔加公主一等勋章——这是该国的最高荣誉之一。他还发出了一个总体要求：“请继续做好你的出色工作并支持人们。”
第一夫人扮演外交官和人道主义者的角色，呼吁“以人道战胜战争”，并表示她希望前线城镇的有限停火能够“激发更大的和平”。
“我们可以共同创造比暂时停火更持久的东西，”她说。 “让我们将奥列什基视为黑暗世界中的一颗火花，能够照亮人类最好的一面。建立世界可见的强大和平之火。点燃希望，促进合作，照亮一条通往持久和平的道路。”
随后，她将私人信件交给德米特里耶夫和阿拉卡米亚，让他们带回给普京和泽连斯基。
唐纳德·特朗普没有出席，周二的日程上也没有任何公共活动。当天晚些时候，他说他会见了迪米特里耶夫，但没有会见乌克兰官员，并拒绝透露他们讨论的内容。总统缺席白宫活动很引人注目，这既是因为出席了备受瞩目的嘉宾，也是因为众所周知，他本人很想被视为和平缔造者。虽然他公开要求获得诺贝尔和平奖，但周四，梅拉尼娅被加冕为人道主义领袖。
这对她来说是一个不寻常的角色。她此前从未参加过乌克兰与俄罗斯之间的高层谈判，据说在幕后一直批评她丈夫对待乌克兰的高压手段。
但她越来越多地参与与冲突相关的人道主义工作，首先是参与一项项目，帮助 30 多名在冲突期间与家人流离失所的儿童团聚。
在奥列什基中，她还声称自己参与了规划的“每个阶段”。她说，为此，她“审查了排雷计划、航拍图像，评估了道路，并讨论了疏散路线、医院通道、车辆和医疗资源”。
现在白宫将她视为黑马外交官。
“这次史无前例的聚会标志着美国历史上第一次由美国第一夫人亲自将两个活跃交战国家的代表聚集在白宫，以追求外交和人道主义目标，”自称是她的独家高级顾问的助手马克·贝克曼(Marc Beckman)说。
显而易见的是，目前双方都认识到有必要让梅拉尼娅和脾气暴躁的特朗普政府站在一边。

title_en: Deep-red Kansas votes for change as patience wears thin with Trump: ‘The economy is really taking a beating’
title_zh: 随着对特朗普的耐心逐渐减弱，深红色的堪萨斯州投票支持变革：“经济确实受到了打击”
summary: Bills have soared in rural state buffeted by tariffs and war in Iran – and Democrat Adam Hamilton’s stunning upset shows how deep economic frustrations run Linda Olson always does her homework before voting – a trait she inherited from a family invested, and i
summary_zh: 受到关税和伊朗战争打击的农村州的账单飙升——民主党人亚当·汉密尔顿的令人震惊的不满表明了经济挫败感有多么严重
body_en: Bills have soared in rural state buffeted by tariffs and war in Iran – and Democrat Adam Hamilton’s stunning upset shows how deep economic frustrations run

L inda Olson always does her homework before voting – a trait she inherited from a family invested, and interested, in politics. Her father was a photographer who took portraits of political leaders in Washington, while her grandparents were farmers who cared deeply about their industry.

In 2024, Olson’s research led her to Donald Trump . She trusted that the then-former president would improve their economic realities in Junction City, Kansas – where she was born and raised – if he returned to the White House.

But two years later, life is just more expensive. Last winter, Olson was forced to spend $700 on medication while in between insurance plans, and skipped out on doses to stretch it out longer. Her grocery bills are unrecognizably high. And fuel prices are about a dollar per gallon more expensive than last year.
“I thought at the time that he was the better choice of what we had,” Olson said of Trump in 2024. Instead, he had been acting to “make himself richer instead of really helping the people”.

With frustrations like these looming large across the state, Kansans this week elected a Democrat, Adam Hamilton, to the US Senate for the first time in nearly a century. It was a stunning upset in what was, until recently, thought to be a reliably red stronghold.
“I’ve seen what Roger Marshall did over the eight years or so that he’s been doing this,” said Olson, of the defeated Republican senator. “And I thought, it’s time we get fresh blood up there.”

Hamilton won, in part, by flipping six counties that backed Trump in 2024 and Marshall in 2020 – a sign that, even in more remote, and traditionally conservative, areas, patience with Trump and the Republican party is wearing thin.

“Not everybody that voted for Trump is part of this cult of personality that Trump has tried to make the Republican party into,” said Michael Smith, a political science professor at Emporia State University, located in one of those six flipped counties.
“There are certainly people in Kansas that are like that: they’re pretty conservative, but they’re not beholden to Trump. And so I think one of the things this election did is peel off those people.”

M ost of Kansas is made up of farmland, encompassing nearly 45m acres and employing nearly one in five Kansans. Pastures, dotted with grazing cows and their calves, hug the state’s highways. Junction City is surrounded by its famed toffee-colored prairies, so expansive that untouched grassland stretches out to the horizon on both sides of the interstate.

Kansans who ranch and farm here, in the most rural corners of the state, remain deeply Republican, according to Smith. But neighboring communities such as Junction City and Emporia, where he teaches, depend heavily on the agricultural economy and have felt the impact of the strains on farmers.
“The people that live here aren’t actually farmers,” he said. “And they’re more likely to swing over to the other party because the economy is really taking a beating.”
David Aguirre, a 25-year-old who was born and raised in Junction City, and works at a Mexican restaurant, El Patron Dos, said that when the rest of the county is suffering, so does his work.
“It has, like, a domino effect for families,” he said. “If they’re not doing their best, they’re not gonna come out to eat, and then that affects staff, and cooks, and so on.”

While grocery shopping on Wednesday afternoon, Janet Grimm, who considers herself an independent, lamented her rising bills. Everything she picked out from the aisles was tagged with a red and yellow “sale” sticker, a conscious choice she needs to make now.
Kansas Democrat’s pitch to voters amid historic Senate bid: ‘I’m gonna just fight like hell’

Checking out with just a handful of items – eggs, chicken, some deli meat, two cucumbers and powdered sugar for the banana bread she was planning on making later that day – her total rang up to over $60.
Grimm voted for Hamilton, and felt hopefully that he would be able to improve the economy for people like her. “I really have faith that they’re going to do good,” she said.
body_zh: 受到关税和伊朗战争打击的农村州的账单飙升——民主党人亚当·汉密尔顿的令人震惊的不满表明了经济挫败感有多么严重
琳达·奥尔森（Linda Olson）总是在投票前做功课——这是她从一个对政治投资和感兴趣的家庭继承的特质。她的父亲是一位摄影师，为华盛顿的政治领导人拍摄肖像，而她的祖父母是农民，非常关心他们的行业。
2024 年，奥尔森的研究让她找到了唐纳德·特朗普。她相信，如果这位时任前总统回到白宫，他将改善她出生和长大的堪萨斯州章克申城的经济现实。
但两年后，生活变得更加昂贵。去年冬天，奥尔森在保险计划期间被迫花费 700 美元购买药物，并且为了延长服药时间而跳过了服药。她的杂货账单高得难以想象。燃油价格比去年每加仑贵一美元左右。
奥尔森在谈到 2024 年的特朗普时说：“我当时认为他是我们所拥有的更好的选择。”相反，他一直在“让自己变得更富有，而不是真正帮助人民”。
由于类似的挫败感在全州范围内日益凸显，堪萨斯州本周选举民主党人亚当·汉密尔顿进入美国参议院，这是近一个世纪以来的首次。对于直到最近还被认为是可靠的红色据点的地方来说，这是一个令人震惊的意外。
“我看到了罗杰·马歇尔在过去八年左右的时间里所做的事情，他一直在这样做，”奥尔森在谈到这位落败的共和党参议员时说道。 “我想，是时候我们为那里注入新鲜血液了。”
汉密尔顿获胜的部分原因是在 2024 年推翻了支持特朗普的六个县，在 2020 年推翻了支持马歇尔的六个县——这表明，即使在更偏远、传统上保守的地区，人们对特朗普和共和党的耐心也在逐渐减弱。
位于这六个翻转县之一的恩波里亚州立大学政治学教授迈克尔·史密斯说：“并不是所有投票给特朗普的人都是特朗普试图让共和党陷入这种个人崇拜的一部分。”
“堪萨斯州肯定有人是这样的：他们相当保守，但他们并不受制于特朗普。所以我认为这次选举所做的事情之一就是剥离了这些人。”
堪萨斯州大部分地区都是农田，占地近 4500 万英亩，雇用了近五分之一的堪萨斯人。牧场紧邻该州的高速公路，牧场上点缀着正在吃草的奶牛和它们的小牛。章克申城周围环绕着著名的太妃糖色大草原，其广阔无垠的草原一直延伸到州际公路两侧的地平线。
史密斯表示，在该州最农村的角落里放牧和务农的堪萨斯人仍然是坚定的共和党人。但他任教的章克申城和恩波里亚等邻近社区严重依赖农业经济，并感受到了农民承受压力的影响。
“住在这里的人实际上并不是农民，”他说。 “而且他们更有可能转向另一方，因为经济确实受到了打击。”
25 岁的戴维·阿吉雷 (David Aguirre) 在章克申城出生和长大，在一家墨西哥餐厅 El Patron Dos 工作，他说，当全县其他人都在受苦时，他的工作也是如此。
“这对家庭来说就像多米诺骨牌效应，”他说。 “如果他们没有尽力而为，他们就不会出来吃饭，这就会影响员工、厨师等。”
周三下午，在杂货店购物时，自认为是独立人士的珍妮特·格林 (Janet Grimm) 对自己不断上涨的账单感到遗憾。她从过道上挑选的所有东西都贴有红色和黄色的“促销”标签，这是她现在需要做出的有意识的选择。
堪萨斯州民主党在历史性的参议院竞选中向选民宣传：“我要拼命战斗”
只检查了几样东西——鸡蛋、鸡肉、一些熟食肉、两根黄瓜和她计划当天晚些时候制作香蕉面包的糖粉——她的总价就超过了 60 美元。
格林投票给了汉密尔顿，并希望他能够为像她这样的人改善经济。 “我真的相信他们会做好事，”她说。

title_zh: 特朗普试图推翻2024年封口费腐败案的定罪

summary_zh: 总统律师要求上诉法院驳回周四发送给斯托米·丹尼尔斯唐纳德·特朗普法律团队的 13 万美元刑事审判判决
body_en: President’s lawyers ask appeals court to toss criminal trial verdict over $130,000 sent to Stormy Daniels
Donald Trump’s legal team on Thursday continued efforts to get his 2024 conviction in the hush-money election corruption case thrown out.

Attorneys for the US president are trying to persuade a New York appeals court to toss the criminal trial verdict from May 2024, when Trump was found guilty on all charges of falsifying business records in the hush-money corruption scheme to influence his eventual victory in the 2016 presidential election .

The felony conviction came after the jury agreed he altered records in order to obscure a $130,000 payment to buy the silence of adult film performer and producer Stormy Daniels . Trump mentioned the case again on social media as recently as September.

He was already the president-elect for his second term in office in early January 2025 when the judge in the case gave Trump an unconditional discharge, meaning he would remain a convicted felon but was given no jail time, fine or other penalty.
The president has always denied any wrongdoing and has turned to state and federal courts in hopes of unwinding the verdict. He was not expected to attend Thursday’s court session.

The trial involved the fee that Daniels received from Trump’s then fixer and lawyer, Michael Cohen , weeks before the 2016 election. The money bought, for a time, her silence about an alleged sexual encounter with Trump a decade earlier when he was already married to Melania Trump and she had given birth to his youngest son, Barron. Trump maintains that nothing sexual happened with Daniels.
However, then Trump’s company reimbursed Cohen in 2017, logging those payments as legal expenses.

Saying the transactions all were meant to keep unflattering information about Trump away from the electorate, prosecutors argue that he “orchestrated a conspiracy” that violated federal campaign finance laws, among others.

Trump’s lawyers argue there is only “weak” evidence that he even knew about Cohen’s dealings at the time. His trial attorneys also said that payments to Cohen were legal expenses and were merely to avoid embarrassing Trump’s family.

On Thursday, a panel of five appellate judges peppered prosecutors and Trump’s lawyer with questions, particularly about the defense’s argument that prosecutors’ legal theory was built on a shaky combination of alleged state and federal offenses.
The Manhattan district attorney’s office says the hush money was meant to keep unflattering information about Trump away from the 2016 electorate and broke the Federal Election Campaign Act (Feca).
Trump lawyer Robert Giuffra Jr told the judges that state prosecutors have no place tying a case to a federal election law. “We think it’s the most obvious ground for reversal,” he said.

Prosecutors argued otherwise, saying that they weren’t prosecuting an alleged federal campaign finance offense, but rather presenting it as a fact that drove what they claim was a conspiracy that led to phony records.
“So are you relying upon Feca in order to prove your falsifying business records (charge)?” asked Troy Webber, the judge.

“Only partially,” replied Steven Wu, the Manhattan assistant district attorney, adding that it was “important only to show that the purpose for the falsifying business records here was to conceal that conspiracy”.

The appeal also concerns whether jurors should have been allowed to hear testimony about supposed White House conversations, workflow and even Trump social media posts during his first term. His lawyers cite presidential immunity for official acts, and they argue his official conduct included responding to the Daniels drama once it became public in 2018.

“When a president addresses the nation to defend himself from allegations of personal misconduct (as all presidents do), or discusses such communications with his aides, he is carrying out his constitutional duties and is protected by immunity,” Giuffra wrote in a filing this October.

Manhattan district attorney Alvin Bragg’s office counters that the legal theory and jury instructions were legitimate and that the White House-related evidence was fair game. Some was public record, some was a general description of office practices, and the conversations were “unofficial conduct”, prosecutors say.
body_zh: 总统律师要求上诉法院驳回向斯托米·丹尼尔斯 (Stormy Daniels) 赔偿 13 万美元的刑事审判判决
周四，唐纳德·特朗普的法律团队继续努力推翻他 2024 年在封口费选举腐败案中的定罪。
美国总统的律师正试图说服纽约上诉法院推翻 2024 年 5 月的刑事审判判决，当时特朗普因在封口费腐败计划中伪造商业记录以影响他在 2016 年总统选举中最终获胜的所有指控而被判有罪。
陪审团同意他篡改记录，以掩盖支付 13 万美元的费用以让成人电影演员兼制片人斯托米·丹尼尔斯保持沉默后，他被判重罪。特朗普就在9月份再次在社交媒体上提到了此案。
2025 年 1 月初，他已经是第二个任期的当选总统，当时该案的法官给予特朗普无条件释放，这意味着他仍将是被定罪的重罪犯，但不会被判处监禁、罚款或其他处罚。
总统一直否认有任何不当行为，并已向州和联邦法院求助，希望能够撤销判决。预计他不会出席周四的法庭会议。
此次审判涉及丹尼尔斯在 2016 年大选前几周从特朗普当时的掮客兼律师迈克尔·科恩那里收到的费用。这笔钱一度让她对十年前与特朗普发生性关系的指控保持沉默，当时特朗普已经与梅拉尼娅·特朗普结婚，她还生下了他最小的儿子巴伦。特朗普坚称丹尼尔斯没有发生性行为。
然而，特朗普的公司在 2017 年向科恩报销了费用，并将这些付款记录为法律费用。
检察官称，这些交易都是为了让选民远离有关特朗普的不雅信息，并认为他“策划了一个阴谋”，违反了联邦竞选财务法等。
特朗普的律师辩称，只有“微弱”的证据表明他当时甚至知道科恩的交易。他的出庭律师还表示，向科恩支付的费用属于法律费用，只是为了避免让特朗普的家人难堪。
周四，一个由五名上诉法官组成的小组向检察官和特朗普的律师提出了很多问题，特别是关于辩方的论点，即检察官的法律理论是建立在被指控的州和联邦罪行的不稳定组合之上的。
曼哈顿地区检察官办公室表示，封口费的目的是让 2016 年选民远离有关特朗普的不雅信息，这违反了《联邦竞选法》(Feca)。
特朗普的律师小罗伯特·朱弗拉 (Robert Giuffra Jr) 告诉法官，州检察官无权将案件与联邦选举法挂钩。 “我们认为这是最明显的逆转理由，”他说。
检察官则反驳说，他们并不是在起诉所谓的联邦竞选财务犯罪，而是将其作为一个事实，推动了他们所说的导致虚假记录的阴谋。
“那么，您是否依靠 Feca 来证明您伪造的业务记录（指控）？”法官特洛伊·韦伯问道。
“只是部分原因，”曼哈顿助理地方检察官史蒂文·吴 (Steven Wu) 回答道，并补充道，“重要的是要表明这里伪造商业记录的目的是为了掩盖这一阴谋”。
该上诉还涉及陪审员是否应该被允许听取关于所谓的白宫对话、工作流程甚至特朗普在第一个任期期间社交媒体帖子的证词。他的律师援引总统对官方行为的豁免权，他们认为他的官方行为包括在丹尼尔斯的戏剧于 2018 年公开后对其做出回应。
朱弗拉在今年 10 月提交的一份文件中写道：“当一位总统向全国发表讲话，为自己免受个人不当行为的指控辩护时（就像所有总统所做的那样），或与他的助手讨论此类沟通时，他正在履行宪法职责，并受到豁免权的保护。”
曼哈顿地区检察官阿尔文·布拉格办公室反驳说，法律理论和陪审团指示是合法的，与白宫相关的证据是公平的。检察官表示，有些是公开记录，有些是对办公室做法的一般描述，而这些对话是“非官方行为”。

title_en: Republicans hoping to succeed Trump in 2028 dissect midterm rout
title_zh: 希望在 2028 年接替特朗普的共和党人剖析中期选举溃败
summary: JD Vance, Ron DeSantis and Ted Cruz all pointed to Iran war and affordability as key factors in Democratic victory US midterms 2026 live – latest updates Republican hopefuls in the race to succeed Donald Trump swiftly blamed two key pillars of his agenda – the
summary_zh: JD Vance、Ron DeSantis 和 Ted Cruz 均指出伊朗战争和负担能力是民主党赢得 2026 年美国中期选举直播的关键因素 – 最新更新
body_en: JD Vance, Ron DeSantis and Ted Cruz all pointed to Iran war and affordability as key factors in Democratic victory

Republican hopefuls in the race to succeed Donald Trump swiftly blamed two key pillars of his agenda – the Iran war and tariffs – for summoning the Democratic blue wave that swept the US midterm elections.

The fallout from the stunning success of Democrats on Tuesday night has left Republicans reeling – and grasping for the reasons behind the collapse in support. On Thursday, the Associated Press called more competitive House races for the Democrats, though Senate races in Alaska and Mississippi remained undecided.

Vice-president JD Vance, the outgoing Florida governor Ron DeSantis , and Texas senator Ted Cruz all pointed to frustration over cost of living amid the fallout from Republican defeats across the country, including in previous strongholds such as Texas and Kansas.
They cited factors including Trump’s prolonged war on Iran and aggressive trade agenda; the US-Israel relationship ; and Democratic ads that painted conservative candidates poorly.
How did Republicans lose a Senate seat in fireball-red South Carolina?

“Tariffs have made everything too expensive and the Iran war has dragged on too long,” Cruz, a former Republican presidential candidate who has not ruled out another run, said on his podcast , Verdict With Ted Cruz, on Wednesday. “It should have been brief, decisive and over. It needs to end.”
“The reason we lost is the war,” Vance wrote in a lengthy X post on Wednesday, suggesting his party lost because voters are angry at the Trump administration for diverting focus away from Americans .
“To the people who are just pissed at the results, you should be,” the vice-president added. “Let’s take that anger and get back to the work of saving our country.”

DeSantis, who unsuccessfully challenged Trump for the Republican nomination two years ago and has since endured a strained relationship with the president, declared this week’s elections to be “close to an extinction-level event” for their party.
Democrats made Republicans look bad with ads targeting them over the case of the convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein and congressional stock trading, DeSantis said on Wednesday .

DeSantis said Republicans had promised they would publish the Epstein files, which included a vast array of documents and correspondences tied to the disgraced financier. He said: “And then you actually have people in the Congress voting against release [of the Epstein files] when the attorney general said she had all this horrific stuff on her desk and that people were going to be held accountable.”

In the months and weeks leading up to the midterms, polling showed voters were increasingly disgruntled with Trump’s handling of his job. Americans were feeling the squeeze of the US economy with gas prices and grocery costs rising – a result of the war with Iran.
Yet Trump remained confident voters would stay loyal to him, encouraging them to vote as though he were on the ballot and campaigning for Republicans in competitive seats.

Democrats, meanwhile, promised to make life more affordable and keep the US president’s sprawling agenda in check – and won over voters. Democrats have seized authority in both chambers of Congress and won a majority of the gubernatorial races around the country.

Tuesday’s results indicate that Trump’s endorsements no longer carry the same power they once did. Several incumbent Republicans that he vouched for in competitive House and Senate races still lost to Democrats.
Though Trump said he would accept the results of the midterms, he quickly deflected, claiming Republicans would have won if his name had actually been on the ballot.

On Thursday, the US president went further, demanding that any votes for Dan J Sullivan, an alternative Republican Senate candidate in Alaska, should go to the incumbent Dan S Sullivan, whom Trump endorsed.

“The vote totals for the Fake Dan Sullivan, plus the other “slug” that the Dems put on the Ballot, should be immediately given to the REAL Dan Sullivan, and the Election is over - He easily wins. There is no other fair solution!” Trump wrote.
body_zh: JD万斯、罗恩德桑蒂斯和特德克鲁兹都指出伊朗战争和负担能力是民主党获胜的关键因素
唐纳德·特朗普(Donald Trump)竞选继任者的共和党人迅速指责其议程的两个关键支柱——伊朗战争和关税——引发了席卷美国中期选举的民主党蓝色浪潮。
周二晚上民主党取得的惊人成功所带来的后果让共和党人感到震惊 — — 并试图找出支持率崩溃背后的原因。周四，美联社呼吁民主党众议院竞选更具竞争力，但阿拉斯加州和密西西比州的参议院竞选仍未决定。
副总统 JD 万斯、即将离任的佛罗里达州州长罗恩·德桑蒂斯和德克萨斯州参议员特德·克鲁兹都指出，共和党在全国范围内失败，包括在德克萨斯州和堪萨斯州等先前的据点，对生活成本感到沮丧。
他们列举的因素包括特朗普对伊朗的长期战争和激进的贸易议程；美国与以色列的关系；民主党广告对保守派候选人的形象描绘不佳。
共和党是如何失去火球红色南卡罗来纳州的参议院席位的？
周三，前共和党总统候选人克鲁兹在他的播客“特德·克鲁兹的判决”中表示，“关税让一切都变得过于昂贵，伊朗战争也拖得太久了。”克鲁兹并未排除再次参选的可能性。 “这应该是简短的、果断的、结束的。它需要结束。”
“我们失败的原因是战争，”万斯周三在一篇长篇 X 帖子中写道，暗示他的政党失败是因为选民对特朗普政府将注意力从美国人身上转移开感到愤怒。
“对于那些只是对结果感到愤怒的人来说，你们应该感到愤怒，”副总统补充道。 “让我们带着愤怒回到拯救我们国家的工作上。”
德桑蒂斯两年前挑战特朗普获得共和党提名，但未能成功，此后一直与总统关系紧张，他宣称本周的选举对该党来说“接近灭绝级别的事件”。
德桑蒂斯周三表示，民主党因被定罪的性犯罪者杰弗里·爱泼斯坦案和国会股票交易而针对共和党人投放广告，让共和党人看起来很糟糕。
德桑蒂斯表示，共和党人已承诺将公布爱泼斯坦的文件，其中包括与这位名誉扫地的金融家有关的大量文件和信件。他说：“当司法部长说她的办公桌上有所有这些可怕的东西并且人们将被追究责任时，国会中实际上有人投票反对公布（爱泼斯坦的文件）。”
在中期选举前的几个月和几周内，民调显示选民对特朗普处理工作的方式越来越不满。由于与伊朗的战争，汽油价格和杂货成本上涨，美国人感受到了美国经济的压力。
然而，特朗普仍然相信选民会保持对他的忠诚，鼓励他们像他一样投票，并在竞争性席位上为共和党竞选。
与此同时，民主党人承诺让人们的生活更加负担得起，并控制美国总统庞大的议程 — — 并赢得了选民的支持。民主党在国会参众两院夺取了权力，并赢得了全国大部分州长竞选的胜利。
周二的结果表明，特朗普的支持不再具有以前那样的力量。他在众议院和参议院竞争激烈的竞选中担保的几位现任共和党人仍然输给了民主党人。
尽管特朗普表示他会接受中期选举的结果，但他很快就改变了态度，声称如果他的名字真的出现在选票上，共和党就会获胜。
周四，美国总统更进一步，要求阿拉斯加州另一位共和党参议员候选人丹·J·沙利文的任何选票都应该投给特朗普支持的现任总统丹·S·沙利文。
“假丹·沙利文的总票数，加上民主党在选票上投入的其他“重头戏”，应该立即给予真正的丹·沙利文，选举就结束了——他轻松获胜。没有其他公平的解决方案！”特朗普写道。

body_en: Sen. Kirsten Gillibrand on Democrats' plans for Congress : NPR

Sen. Kirsten Gillibrand on Democrats' plans for Congress Sen. Kirsten Gillibrand spoke with Morning Edition about Democrats' priorities, from lowering costs to ending the Iran war. But questions remain about how they'll deliver.
Sen. Kirsten Gillibrand on the Democratic Party's agenda for the next Congress
Sen. Kirsten Gillibrand, D-N.Y., attends a Senate Armed Services Committee hearing in Washington on April 30, 2026. Graeme Sloan/Getty Images hide caption
Back in the majority, Democrats have plans for a long list of Trump investigations
Democrats have won back Congress. Now comes the harder question: How much can they actually change with President Trump still in the White House?
"I dare him to veto that," Sen. Kirsten Gillibrand of New York told Morning Edition , challenging Trump to reject bipartisan legislation restoring Medicaid coverage.
Does the blue wave mean lower gasoline and diesel prices soon? Don't hold your breath
Gillibrand said Democrats would focus on lowering costs, restoring health care access and ending the war in Iran.
Democrats also face pressure to hold the Trump administration accountable, with new investigative powers and the possibility of a third impeachment.
Asked about impeachment, Gillibrand did not commit to pursuing it.
"We can do both," she said, proposing a ban on stock trading by members of Congress and senior administration officials.
U.S. and Israel are planning for a possible attack on Iran, source tells NPR
Like other Democrats, Gillibrand cited the war in Iran as a factor in the party's election victories, saying Trump had broken his promise to avoid prolonged wars as the conflict drove up costs.

Trump acknowledged Wednesday that the war had contributed to Republicans' election losses. But the conflict continues, with Iranian officials warning against renewed U.S. attacks. How Democrats intend to bring the war to an end remains unclear.
In her interview with NPR's A Martínez, Gillibrand also discussed Democrats' gains in Republican states, Trump's ballroom and cuts to food assistance and medical research.

“我们可以两者兼顾，”她说，并提议禁止国会议员和高级政府官员进行股票交易。
消息人士告诉美国国家公共广播电台，美国和以色列正在计划对伊朗发动可能的袭击

title_en: How Abdul El-Sayed actually did with Jewish voters
title_zh: 阿卜杜勒·赛义德实际上是如何对待犹太选民的
summary: Yes, he ran behind. In an interview, the senator-elect acknowledged Israel was a source of disagreement, but said he’s not changing his position.
summary_zh: 是的，他跑到了后面。在接受采访时，当选参议员承认以色列是分歧的根源，但表示他不会改变立场。
body_en: Abdul El-Sayed ran well behind other Michigan Democrats in places with more Jewish voters, according to a detailed POLITICO analysis of precinct-level results.

Statewide, the progressive senator-elect only ran two points behind Democratic Gov.-elect Jocelyn Benson, getting 52.5% of the vote compared to her 54.5%. But the gap was much larger in heavily Jewish communities: In Huntington Woods, a Detroit suburb that is roughly two-thirds Jewish, El-Sayed ran nearly 15 points behind Benson, getting 65.3% of the vote compared to Benson’s 80%.
In West Bloomfield, the site of the March synagogue attack that shook the Senate primary and a town where roughly a quarter of residents are Jewish, El-Sayed ran 8.8 points behind Benson.

El-Sayed faced blowback from some Jewish Democrats during his campaign, particularly over his calls to end U.S. military support to Israel and his remarks after the synagogue attack that “hurt people hurt people,” for which he later apologized .
El-Sayed, who will be the first Muslim senator in U.S. history, told POLITICO on Wednesday that he hoped he could “earn support” from Jewish voters who hadn’t backed him in this election.

“One of the big issues of disagreement that kept showing up when it came to the Jewish community was my position on Israel,” El-Sayed said. “I'm not going to change my position, but …I intend to lead on all the issues that we agree on — whether it's the right to a union or the right to health care, clean air, clean water, or religious pluralism, and respect for the Constitution — and I hope that over time I can earn [their] support on those issues.”

El-Sayed had worked to make inroads with Jewish voters over the course of his campaign, pledging to stand up to antisemitism and for Jewish safety. Still, some Jewish leaders and activists in the state urged voters to blank their ballots in the Senate race, or back Republican former Rep. Mike Rogers.

His former Democratic primary rival, Rep. Haley Stevens, also switched her endorsement from El-Sayed to Rogers days before the election, citing concerns over antisemitism and the Democrat and his allies’ views and rhetoric around Israel. She pointed to an ad put out by a prominent El-Sayed supporter tying high grocery prices to U.S. aid to Israel, which El-Sayed and his campaign distanced themselves from.

Jewish voters, who make up roughly 1.4% of the Michigan electorate, have historically backed Democrats by large margins. But disagreements over support for Israel and how the party should respond to rising antisemitism are testing that voting bloc — both in Michigan and across the country.
A poll of Jewish early voters in the state found that a majority still backed El-Sayed, but roughly one in four who had supported Sen. Elissa Slotkin in 2024 switched to back Rogers.

With Michigan in Democrats’ early primary window for 2028, El-Sayed said his statewide win showed voters were aligned with his positioning on Israel — and that he hopes the next presidential nominee takes note.

“If you want to be where the voters are, if you want to be on the side of peace and on the side of justice and transparency, I believe that that is around holding Israel accountable to its war crimes and on making sure our tax dollars get used to do good things here rather than bad things somewhere else,” he said.

In a post-election memo , El-Sayed’s campaign touted an outside analysis finding that he only ran slightly behind Slotkin’s 2024 performance in predominantly Jewish precincts. The memo also noted he was outspent heavily in both the primary and general elections, including by “MAGA billionaires, AIPAC, Elon Musk, and corporate interests determined to elect candidates who would defend the status quo.”

But he won in a blue wave while Slotkin, who is Jewish, overcame a tough year. El-Sayed’s margins were far better than Slotkin’s numbers across nearly all of the state, suggesting Jewish voters moved in the opposite direction of most Michiganders.

On the other hand, El-Sayed particularly surged in areas with more Muslim voters, who make up roughly 2.4% of Michigan’s electorate. In Dearborn, for example, he won 82.5% of the vote compared to 78.7% for Benson. Two years ago, Slotkin won 41.4% in the city while former Vice President Kamala Harris received just 36.3% of the vote.

Lansing Mayor Andy Schor, a Jewish Democrat who supported Stevens in the primary and did not endorse El-Sayed, said he was unsurprised by that split screen. He expressed hope about El-Sayed’s relationship with the Jewish community going forward, but also said Jewish leaders should continue to raise their concerns to the incoming senator.
“Everybody has to keep talking to him. His views aren’t going to change, and we know what they are,” Schor said. But, “I hope he’s open to hearing the concerns of some of his constituents.”

Nonnegotiable Michigan, a group of Jewish activists that pushed El-Sayed on issues of Jewish safety and Israel, also said in a postelection statement that it was “prepared to work with” El-Sayed “even as we continue to hold elected leaders accountable when antisemitism enters our politics or political discourse.”
El-Sayed made clear he has no plans to change his views on Israel, but said he will be straight with voters — and that he’ll “show up for you when you need me” regardless of their differences.

“With me, what you see is what you get. And I've never once gone and told somebody that I was anything but what I am,” El-Sayed said Wednesday. “We're going to disagree. I'm going to be honest, specific and direct. And over time, I hope that I can earn support for leading on the issues on which I hope to lead and [by] serving everybody.”
body_zh: 根据《政治》杂志对选区一级结果的详细分析，阿卜杜勒·赛义德在犹太选民较多的地方远远落后于其他密歇根州民主党人。
在全州范围内，这位进步派当选参议员仅落后民主党州长当选人乔斯林·本森 (Jocelyn Benson) 两分，她获得了 52.5% 的选票，而她的得票率为 54.5%。但在犹太人口较多的社区，这种差距要大得多：在大约三分之二是犹太人的底特律郊区亨廷顿伍兹，埃尔-赛义德落后本森近 15 个百分点，获得了 65.3% 的选票，而本森只有 80%。
在西布卢姆菲尔德，三月犹太教堂袭击事件震惊了参议院初选，该镇约有四分之一的居民是犹太人，埃尔-赛义德的支持率落后本森 8.8 个百分点。
埃尔赛义德在竞选期间遭到了一些犹太民主党人的反击，特别是他呼吁结束美国对以色列的军事支持，以及他在犹太教堂袭击后发表的“伤人伤人”的言论，他后来为此道歉。
埃尔-赛义德将成为美国历史上第一位穆斯林参议员，他周三告诉《政治》杂志，他希望自己能够“赢得”在这次选举中不支持他的犹太选民的支持。
“当谈到犹太社区时，不断出现的重大分歧问题之一是我对以色列的立场，”埃尔赛义德说。 “我不会改变我的立场，但是……我打算在我们同意的所有问题上发挥领导作用——无论是工会权还是医疗保健权、清洁空气、清洁水或宗教多元化，以及尊重宪法——我希望随着时间的推移，我能够在这些问题上赢得[他们]的支持。”
埃尔-赛义德在竞选过程中一直努力争取犹太选民的支持，承诺抵制反犹太主义并维护犹太人的安全。尽管如此，该州的一些犹太领袖和活动人士仍敦促选民在参议院竞选中留白选票，或支持共和党前众议员迈克·罗杰斯。
他的前民主党主要竞争对手、众议员海莉·史蒂文斯也在选举前几天将她的支持从埃尔·赛义德转为罗杰斯，理由是对反犹太主义以及民主党及其盟友围绕以色列的观点和言论的担忧。她指出，一位著名的赛义德支持者发布的一则广告将高杂货价格与美国对以色列的援助挂钩，赛义德和他的竞选团队与此保持距离。
犹太选民约占密歇根州选民的 1.4%，历来以大幅优势支持民主党。但在支持以色列以及该党应如何应对日益高涨的反犹太主义方面存在的分歧正在考验这个投票集团——无论是在密歇根州还是在全国各地。
对该州犹太早期选民的一项民意调查发现，大多数人仍然支持埃尔-赛义德，但大约四分之一的 2024 年支持参议员埃丽莎·斯洛特金的人转而支持罗杰斯。
密歇根州正处于民主党 2028 年的早期初选窗口，埃尔-赛义德表示，他在全州范围内的胜利表明选民与他对以色列的立场一致，他希望下一任总统候选人能够注意到这一点。
他说：“如果你想站在选民的立场上，如果你想站在和平一边，站在正义和透明一边，我认为那就是让以色列对其战争罪行负责，并确保我们的税款在这里用来做好事，而不是在其他地方做坏事。”
在一份选举后的备忘录中，埃尔·赛义德的竞选团队吹捧了一项外部分析结果，该分析发现，他在 2024 年在犹太人占主导地位的选区的表现仅略落后于斯洛特金。备忘录还指出，他在初选和大选中的支出都超过了他，其中包括“MAGA 亿万富翁、AIPAC、埃隆·马斯克和决心选举捍卫现状的候选人的企业利益集团”。
但他在蓝色浪潮中获胜，而犹太人斯洛特金则克服了艰难的一年。在几乎全州范围内，埃尔-赛义德的支持率远高于斯洛特金的支持率，这表明犹太选民的投票方向与大多数密歇根人相反。
另一方面，埃尔-赛义德在穆斯林选民较多的地区尤其飙升，穆斯林选民约占密歇根州选民的 2.4%。例如，在迪尔伯恩，他赢得了 82.5% 的选票，而本森赢得了 78.7% 的选票。两年前，斯洛特金在该市赢得了 41.4% 的选票，而前副总统卡马拉·哈里斯 (Kamala Harris) 仅获得 36.3% 的选票。
兰辛市市长安迪·肖尔（Andy Schor）是一名犹太民主党人，他在初选中支持史蒂文斯，但不支持埃尔·赛义德。他表示，他对分屏并不感到惊讶。他对埃尔赛义德与犹太社区的关系未来发展表示希望，但也表示犹太领导人应继续向即将上任的参议员提出他们的担忧。
“每个人都必须继续与他交谈。他的观点不会改变，我们知道这些观点是什么，”肖尔说。但是，“我希望他愿意倾听一些选民的担忧。”
不可谈判的密歇根州是一个在犹太安全和以色列问题上推动埃尔赛义德的犹太活动家组织，该组织也在一份选举后声明中表示，它“准备与”埃尔赛义德合作，“即使当反犹太主义进入我们的政治或政治话语时，我们仍将继续追究民选领导人的责任”。
埃尔-赛义德明确表示，他不打算改变对以色列的看法，但表示他将坦诚地对待选民，并且无论选民之间存在分歧，他都会“在你们需要我的时候出现在你们身边”。
“对我来说，所见即所得。我从来没有告诉过别人我不是我，”埃尔-赛义德周三说道。 “我们会不同意。我会诚实、具体和直接。随着时间的推移，我希望我能够赢得支持，以领导我希望领导和服务所有人的问题。”

WASHINGTON (AP) — Corruption topped the list of concerns for voters who ousted Republicans and handed Democrats control of Congress in the midterm elections. Now, the newly empowered Democratic Party is putting the issue front and center as its leaders chart their course for investigations and policymaking.

Senior Democrats in both chambers of Congress have vowed to marshal the subpoena powers and larger investigative staffs that come with their soon-to-be majorities to probe what they say is the self-enrichment that President Donald Trump and people in his orbit have done at the public's expense. The Republican president and his White House have long denied any wrongdoing.
WATCH: Tracking the Trump family's business deals and profits in his 2nd term

House Democrats are preparing a vast oversight agenda to look at how Trump and his family have become wealthier since he returned to office — and Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries of New York, who's in line to become House speaker, has not ruled out trying to impeach Trump for a third time.

Months ago, Jeffries tasked the ranking Democrats on the Oversight and Judiciary committees, Rep. Robert Garcia of California and Rep. Jamie Raskin of Maryland, with leading the effort, as Democrats work to link the costs of public corruption to the affordability concerns hitting Americans' pocketbooks.
"Lawyer up," Garcia posted on X as election results favoring Democrats began coming in on Tuesday night.
The Senate is expected to conduct similar investigations.

"Americans want us to clean up corruption in government," said Sen. Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., who is poised to return as Senate majority leader next year. "No American should have to make tradeoffs at the supermarket while Trump is making inside trades on the stock market."
Investigation targets could include ICE raids, Epstein and DOGE

Garcia, the top Democrat on the Oversight and Government Reform Committee, has outlined five priorities, including Trump family business dealings, the administration's handling of the Jeffrey Epstein investigation and Immigration and Customs Enforcement operations. Rep. Jared Huffman of California, the ranking Democrat on the Natural Resources Committee, said he wants to dig into Trump's White House ballroom and other construction projects, as well as the Trump family's role in mineral deals.

With the House majority comes an infusion of congressional committee staff and resources, and the effort is expected to be sprawling, involving House committees with authority to conduct oversight on Cabinet officials and the agencies they lead.

In the Senate, Sen. Richard Blumenthal, D-Conn., who is expected to become the chairman of the Homeland Security Committee's Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations, said his panel will want to look into Trump's real estate projects around the nation's capital and his crypto dealings with special envoy Steve Witkoff. Witkoff is a longtime ally who partnered with Trump on the president's family cryptocurrency venture, World Liberty Financial.

"The tentacles of corruption reach deep in this administration, and they have added costs to everyday Americans," Blumenthal said in an interview with The Associated Press on Wednesday. The senator added that he also wants hearings on ICE raids, the actions of the Department of Government Efficiency and Medicare plans he says are too restrictive and have cost some patients care.

Meanwhile, Democratic Sen. Ron Wyden of Oregon, who is in line to become Senate Finance Committee chairman, ticked off several investigative targets that he describes as part of an "accountability" agenda, including banks that he contends ignored red flags about the financial dealings of Epstein and pharmaceutical companies that have profited from their ties to the Trump administration.
"When I am chair, they will be forced to answer to the Senate Finance Committee for their role in hurting the American people and enabling Trump's corruption," Wyden said in a statement Wednesday.
body_zh: 金承敏 (Seung Min Kim)，美联社 金承敏 (Seung Min Kim)，美联社
玛丽·克莱尔·贾洛尼克（美联社） 玛丽·克莱尔·贾洛尼克（美联社）
华盛顿（美联社）——在中期选举中，腐败问题成为选民最关心的问题，他们推翻了共和党，将国会控制权交给了民主党。现在，新获得权力的民主党领导人正在制定调查和政策制定路线，将这一问题置于首要和中心位置。
国会参众两院的资深民主党人发誓要调动传票权和更大规模的调查人员，他们将与即将成为多数派的人一起调查他们所说的唐纳德·特朗普总统和他身边的人以公众利益为代价实现自我致富的行为。这位共和党总统和他的白宫长期以来一直否认有任何不当行为。
观看：追踪特朗普家族在第二任期内的商业交易和利润
众议院民主党人正在准备一项庞大的监督议程，以了解特朗普及其家人自他重返办公室以来如何变得更加富有——而即将成为众议院议长的纽约民主党领袖哈基姆·杰弗里斯（Hakeem Jeffries）并不排除尝试第三次弹劾特朗普。
几个月前，杰弗里斯责成监督和司法委员会的高级民主党人、加州众议员罗伯特·加西亚和马里兰州众议员杰米·拉斯金领导这项工作，因为民主党正在努力将公共腐败成本与美国人钱包承受能力的担忧联系起来。
“律师起来，”加西亚在周二晚上开始公布有利于民主党的选举结果时在 X 上发帖。
预计参议院将进行类似的调查。
纽约州民主党参议员查克·舒默 (Chuck Schumer) 表示：“美国人希望我们清理政府中的腐败行为。”他准备于明年再次担任参议院多数党领袖。 “当特朗普在股市进行内幕交易时，任何美国人都不应该在超市进行权衡。”
调查目标可能包括 ICE 突袭、爱泼斯坦和 DOGE
监督和政府改革委员会的民主党最高领导人加西亚概述了五个优先事项，包括特朗普家族企业交易、政府对杰弗里·爱泼斯坦调查的处理以及移民和海关执法行动。自然资源委员会资深民主党人、加利福尼亚州众议员贾里德·霍夫曼表示，他希望深入研究特朗普的白宫舞厅和其他建筑项目，以及特朗普家族在矿产交易中的作用。
随着众议院获得多数席位，国会委员会的工作人员和资源将不断注入，预计这项工作将是广泛的，包括有权对内阁官员及其领导的机构进行监督的众议院委员会。
在参议院，预计将成为国土安全委员会常设调查小组委员会主席的康涅狄格州民主党参议员理查德·布卢门撒尔表示，他的小组将希望调查特朗普在首都周边的房地产项目以及他与特使史蒂夫·威特科夫的加密货币交易。威特科夫是特朗普的长期盟友，曾与特朗普合作创办总统的家族加密货币企业世界自由金融公司。
布卢门撒尔周三在接受美联社采访时表示：“腐败的触角深入到本届政府，它们增加了普通美国人的成本。”这位参议员补充说，他还希望就 ICE 突击搜查、政府效率部的行动以及医疗保险计划举行听证会，他认为医疗保险计划过于严格，导致一些患者失去了护理费用。
与此同时，即将成为参议院金融委员会主席的俄勒冈州民主党参议员罗恩·怀登(Ron Wyden)列出了几个调查目标，他将其描述为“问责”议程的一部分，其中包括他认为无视爱泼斯坦金融交易危险信号的银行，以及从与特朗普政府的关系中获利的制药公司。
怀登在周三的一份声明中表示：“当我担任主席时，他们将被迫向参议院财政委员会负责，因为他们在伤害美国人民和助长特朗普腐败方面发挥了作用。”

title_en: Trump's arch is on the verge of federal approval. But a judge could block construction
title_zh: 特朗普的拱门即将获得联邦批准。但法官可以阻止建设
summary: A federal panel will meet to consider the arch for final approval on Thursday, and the government said it may begin construction later that same day. Critics hope a judge will intervene last-minute.
summary_zh: 联邦小组将于周四开会审议拱门的最终批准，政府表示可能会在当天晚些时候开始施工。
body_en: Trump's arch nears approval, but judge could block construction : NPR

Trump's arch nears approval, but judge could block construction A federal panel will meet to consider the arch for final approval on Thursday, and the government said it may begin construction later that same day. Critics hope a judge will intervene last-minute.

The government submitted final renderings to the National Capital Planning Commission that depict a 250-foot arch topped with three gold statues and an eternal flame. Department of the Interior hide caption
Thursday could be a make-or-break day for President Trump's triumphal arch.

For months, the Trump administration has barreled toward his dream of building a 250-foot arch in Washington, D.C.: rubber-stamping and side-stepping various federal reviews, cutting out Congress and announcing imminent construction despite a lack of final approval and an ongoing legal battle.

In May, the entirely Trump-appointed Commission for Fine Arts approved the arch's design — still incomplete at the time . In September, a federal council packed with Trump allies abruptly terminated a historic preservation review that participants had already criticized as rushed .
As Trump's proposed arch looms over D.C., protesters pin their hopes on the midterms

It all comes to a head on Thursday, when the National Capital Planning Commission will meet to consider final approval for the controversial structure. The arch is the only item on the agenda; the meeting will be online-only and is expected to take five hours because of the high volume of public participation.

More than 130 concerned citizens have signed up to speak, an unusually high number for such meetings and a symbol of the widespread public opposition. Democratic lawmakers, veterans, historic preservationists and more than 100,000 people have spoken out against the arch in written comments, local protests and previous commission meetings.

Among their many concerns , critics say the structure would obstruct an important view , insult service members buried on the hallowed ground of nearby Arlington National Cemetery and add a layer of risk to notoriously complicated D.C. airspace. They see the arch as part of Trump's unilateral effort to memorialize himself in the nation's capital.

The White House has repeatedly said the arch will "enhance the visitor experience at Arlington National Cemetery" and be "one of the most iconic landmarks not only in Washington, D.C., but throughout the world."
Veterans and relatives see no place for Trump's arch near Arlington National Cemetery

"It will be one of the great things we've ever done," Trump said from the Reflecting Pool on Monday, giving the arch — alongside several other D.C. construction projects — valuable airtime in his last in-person remarks before the midterm elections.

The planning commission is widely expected to greenlight the arch. It approved preliminary site and building plans over the summer, and its new Trump-appointed chair, Mark Paoletta, expressed his enthusiastic support for the arch in an op-ed published last month. The administration says that after a successful commission vote, all that's needed to break ground is sign-off from its own Department of the Interior .
In fact, the government notified a federal judge late last month that, pending those two approvals, "construction could commence as early as" Thursday.

Trump wants to build his arch on the grassy traffic circle on Arlington Memorial Bridge, between the Lincoln Memorial and Arlington National Cemetery (the entrance to which is seen in the background). The house on the top of the hill formerly belonged to Confederate Gen. Robert E. Lee. Saul Loeb/Pool/AFP via Getty Images hide caption

It filed that notice as part of the ongoing lawsuit brought by Vietnam War veterans and an architectural historian who argue the arch is unlawful without approval from Congress. The Trump administration has not sought that, instead citing Congress' century-old authorization of a pair of columns on that traffic circle that were ultimately never built.

The plaintiffs promptly asked District Judge Tanya Chutkan to issue a preliminary injunction before Thursday's meeting to block the administration from "taking any steps to construct, or to direct or facilitate construction, of any structure in Memorial Circle, absent congressional authorization" while the case plays out.
Trump aims to leave a physical legacy in D.C., bulldozing norms along the way
body_zh: 特朗普的拱门即将获得批准，但法官可能会阻止施工：NPR
特朗普的拱门即将获得批准，但法官可能会阻止施工联邦小组将于周四开会审议拱门的最终批准，政府表示可能会在当天晚些时候开始施工。批评者希望法官能在最后一刻介入。
政府向国家首都规划委员会提交了最终效果图，其中描绘了一个 250 英尺高的拱门，顶部有三座金色雕像和永恒的火焰。内政部隐藏标题栏
周四对于特朗普总统的凯旋门来说可能是决定成败的一天。
几个月来，特朗普政府一直在努力实现在华盛顿特区建造一座 250 英尺拱门的梦想：橡皮图章并回避各种联邦审查，排除国会的影响，并宣布即将施工，尽管缺乏最终批准且正在进行的法律斗争。
五月，完全由特朗普任命的美术委员会批准了拱门的设计——当时尚未完成。 9月，由特朗普盟友组成的联邦委员会突然终止了一项历史保护审查，与会者批评这项审查仓促。
随着特朗普提议的拱门笼罩在华盛顿特区，抗议者将希望寄托在中期选举上
这一切都在周四达到了紧要关头，届时国家首都规划委员会将开会考虑对这一有争议的结构的最终批准。拱门是议程上唯一的项目；由于公众参与人数众多，会议将仅在线进行，预计将持续五个小时。
超过 130 名关心此事的公民已报名发言，此类会议的人数异常之多，也是公众普遍反对的象征。民主党议员、退伍军人、历史保护主义者和超过 10 万人在书面评论、当地抗议和之前的委员会会议中公开反对这座拱门。
批评人士担心，该建筑会阻碍重要景观，侮辱埋葬在附近阿灵顿国家公墓神圣土地上的军人，并给臭名昭著的复杂的华盛顿特区空域增加一层风险。他们认为这座拱门是特朗普单方面在国家首都纪念自己的努力的一部分。
白宫多次表示，这座拱门将“增强阿灵顿国家公墓的游客体验”，并成为“不仅是华盛顿特区，而且是全世界最具标志性的地标之一”。
退伍军人和亲属认为阿灵顿国家公墓附近没有特朗普拱门的位置
特朗普周一在倒影池说道：“这将是我们做过的最伟大的事情之一。”在中期选举前的最后一次亲自讲话中，特朗普为这座拱门以及华盛顿特区的其他几个建设项目提供了宝贵的播出时间。
人们普遍预计规划委员会将为这座拱门开绿灯。它在今年夏天批准了初步选址和建筑计划，特朗普任命的新任主席马克·保莱塔(Mark Paoletta)在上个月发表的一篇专栏文章中表达了他对拱门的热情支持。政府表示，在委员会成功投票后，破土动工所需的只是得到内政部的批准。
事实上，政府上个月末通知一位联邦法官，在等待这两项批准之前，“施工最早可能于周四开始”。
特朗普希望在林肯纪念堂和阿灵顿国家公墓之间的阿灵顿纪念大桥的绿草如茵的交通环岛上建造他的拱门（背景中可以看到其入口）。山顶上的房子以前属于南方联盟将军罗伯特·E·李 (Robert E. Lee)。 Saul Loeb/Pool/法新社来自 Getty Images 隐藏标题栏
该公司提交的通知是越南战争退伍军人和建筑历史学家正在进行的诉讼的一部分，他们认为未经国会批准该拱门是非法的。特朗普政府并没有寻求这一点，而是援引了国会百年前的授权，在该交通圈上修建了两根立柱，但最终从未建成。
原告立即要求地区法官塔尼娅·查特坎 (Tanya Chutkan) 在周四的会议之前发布初步禁令，阻止政府在案件审理期间“在未经国会授权的情况下，采取任何措施在纪念圈内建造、指导或协助建造任何建筑物”。
特朗普的目标是在华盛顿留下物质遗产，一路推倒规范

title_en: The South flexes political power in midterms, sets regional influence in 2028 election
title_zh: 南方在中期选举中展示政治权力，在 2028 年选举中确定地区影响力
summary: Tuesday's dramatic midterm results have transformed the electoral map, ensuring the path to future power for Democrats and Republicans must run through the South and its diverse voting population.
summary_zh: 周二戏剧性的中期结果改变了选举版图，确保民主党和共和党的未来权力之路必须贯穿始终
body_en: Georgia Gov.-elect Keisha Lance Bottoms speaks during an election night watch party on Nov. 3 in Atlanta. Bottoms will be the nation's first Black woman governor. Megan Varner/Getty Images hide caption
Tuesday's dramatic midterm results have transformed the electoral map, ensuring the future path to power for Democrats and Republicans alike must run through the South.
Black voter turnout surged in states like Louisiana and Georgia, as Democrats flipped Senate seats in North Carolina, South Carolina and Texas. Mississippi is too close to call.

Republican-led efforts to redraw House districts to gain more favorable districts in places like Alabama, North Carolina, Texas and Florida backfired, with Democrats poised to net several seats in the region.

In several states, the margins at the top of the ticket were so large that the blue tsunami carried down-ballot races along with it, flipping several state legislative chambers and statewide offices along the way.

Even in contests where Democrats ultimately did not prevail, the millions of dollars of investment from both sides and the wide-ranging repudiation of the Trump administration from every demographic group highlight the South's important role in control of Congress and the White House in future election cycles.

In the aftermath of a Supreme Court ruling earlier this year that gutted part of the Voting Rights Act, Republican-led Southern states rushed to redraw House maps to create additional seats that would better withstand a midterm environment where voters punished the party in power.

They included changes in Tennessee that split Memphis into three districts (and where Democratic state Rep. Justin Pearson is within a few thousand votes of winning), a redraw of several Alabama districts that sought to unseat Rep. Shomari Figures (who won by nearly 8 points in the new Trump +14 configuration) and a target of nine seats in Texas and Florida.
As of Wednesday night, Republicans have won one of them, according to a race call by the Associated Press.

Before Election Day, there were signs that the ruling, along with the war in Iran, rising costs, concerns about corruption with the Trump administration and other top issues would serve as a motivator for turnout among Black voters.
See how Latinos, young voters and other demographic groups fueled Democrats' big wins

In primaries held after the ruling, Black voter participation soared. Ashley Kennedy Shelton with the Louisiana-based Power Coalition for Equity and Justice previously told NPR that the court decision was "personal" for Black voters.

"Everybody's spending more money on their electricity bills, their gas bills, their food bills," she said. "All of these different things are really personally impacting voters. And I think that for all the folks that used to say, 'I don't do politics!' I think they realize that politics is absolutely doing them, and they have to get involved."

In South Carolina, where Democrat Annie Andrews flipped a U.S. Senate seat, the state saw record voting for a gubernatorial election year, driven in part by elevated Black turnout. It's a similar story in Louisiana, where Democrat Jamie Davis narrowly lost to Sen.-elect Julia Letlow by less than 2% in a state President Trump won by more than 15 points in 2024.

Mississippi's Senate race is too close to call, with Democrat Scott Colom leading by less than 1,200 votes against incumbent Republican Cindy Hyde-Smith in a state with the highest share of Black voters in the country.

It's not just Congress where the South is the center of shifting power. Big Democratic victories — or swings away from Republicans — at the top of the ticket led to an avalanche of shifting offices at the state and local level.

Democratic Sen. Jon Ossoff's 18-point victory in Georgia helped propel former Atlanta Mayor Keisha Lance Bottoms to victory in the governor's race, as Democrats swept every single statewide elected office, gained control of the state utility regulator, and are set to win a majority in the state House.
In this file photo from the 2026 election, people wait to vote in early voting for the midterm elections on Oct. 25 in Cary, N.C. Allison Joyce/AFP via Getty Images hide caption
In North Carolina, former Gov. Roy Cooper's 20-point victory was enough to potentially flip multiple congressional seats and win control of the state House.
body_zh: 佐治亚州当选州长凯莎·兰斯·博顿斯 (Keisha Lance Bottoms) 于 11 月 3 日在亚特兰大举行的选举守夜派对上发表讲话。博特克斯将成为美国第一位黑人女州长。梅根瓦尔纳/盖蒂图片社隐藏标题栏
周二戏剧性的中期结果改变了选举版图，确保民主党和共和党未来的权力之路都必须经过南方。
随着民主党翻转北卡罗来纳州、南卡罗来纳州和德克萨斯州的参议院席位，路易斯安那州和佐治亚州等州的黑人选民投票率激增。密西西比州太近了，无法打电话。
共和党主导的重新划分众议院选区的努力，以在阿拉巴马州、北卡罗来纳州、得克萨斯州和佛罗里达州等地获得更有利的选区，但结果适得其反，民主党准备在该地区赢得多个席位。
在几个州，选票顶部的差距如此之大，以至于蓝色海啸也随之带来了下一轮选票的竞争，一路上掀翻了几个州立法机构和全州办公室。
即使在民主党最终没有获胜的竞选中，双方数百万美元的投资以及各个人口群体对特朗普政府的广泛否认也凸显了南方在未来选举周期中控制国会和白宫的重要作用。
今年早些时候，最高法院裁决废除了《投票权法案》的一部分，之后，共和党领导的南方各州急忙重新绘制众议院地图，以创造更多席位，以更好地承受选民惩罚执政党的中期环境。
其中包括田纳西州的改革，将孟菲斯分为三个选区（民主党州众议员贾斯汀·皮尔逊距离获胜只有几千票），重新抽签阿拉巴马州的几个选区，试图取代众议员肖马里·图斯（在新的特朗普+14配置中，他以近8个百分点获胜），以及德克萨斯州和佛罗里达州的九个席位的目标。
据美联社的竞选呼吁，截至周三晚上，共和党赢得了其中一场胜利。
在选举日之前，有迹象表明，这项裁决以及伊朗战争、成本上升、对特朗普政府腐败的担忧以及其他首要问题将成为黑人选民投票率的动力。
了解拉丁裔、年轻选民和其他人口群体如何推动民主党取得重大胜利
在裁决后举行的初选中，黑人选民的参与度飙升。总部位于路易斯安那州的公平与正义权力联盟的阿什利·肯尼迪·谢尔顿此前告诉美国公共广播电台，法院的决定对黑人选民来说是“个人的”。
“每个人都在电费、煤气费和食品费上花更多的钱，”她说。 “所有这些不同的事情都确实对选民产生了个人影响。我认为对于所有过去常说‘我不参与政治！’的人来说也是如此。”我认为他们意识到政治绝对在影响他们，他们必须参与其中。”
在南卡罗来纳州，民主党人安妮·安德鲁斯(Annie Andrews)推翻了美国参议院席位，该州州长选举年的投票率创历史新高，部分原因是黑人投票率上升。路易斯安那州的情况也类似，民主党人杰米·戴维斯 (Jamie Davis) 以不到 2% 的微弱优势输给了当选参议员朱莉娅·莱特洛 (Julia Letlow)，而特朗普总统在 2024 年以超过 15 个百分点的优势获胜。
密西西比州的参议院竞选势均力敌，民主党人斯科特·科洛姆(Scott Colom)以不到1,200票的优势领先于现任共和党人辛迪·海德-史密斯(Cindy Hyde-Smith)，该州是该州黑人选民比例最高的州。
南方不仅是国会，也是权力转移的中心。民主党在选票上的巨大胜利——或者说与共和党的对立——导致州和地方层面的办公室发生雪崩式的变动。
民主党参议员乔恩·奥索夫 (Jon Ossoff) 在佐治亚州以 18 个百分点的优势获胜，帮助亚特兰大前市长凯莎·兰斯·博顿斯 (Keisha Lance Bottoms) 在州长竞选中获胜，民主党席卷了全州所有民选办公室，控制了州公用事业监管机构，并有望在州议会赢得多数席位。
在这张 2026 年选举的资料照片中，人们等待 10 月 25 日在北卡罗来纳州卡里为中期选举提前投票。Allison Joyce/法新社（来自 Getty Images）隐藏标题栏
在北卡罗来纳州，前州长罗伊·库珀 (Roy Cooper) 赢得 20 个百分点的胜利，足以推翻多个国会席位并赢得州议会的控制权。

title_en: Democratic socialist Nithya Raman wins Los Angeles mayoral race over incumbent Karen Bass
title_zh: 民主社会主义者尼西亚·拉曼 (Nithya Raman) 击败现任凯伦·巴斯 (Karen Bass) 赢得洛杉矶市长竞选
summary: Major shake-up as LA councilmember, once considered long shot, ousts Democratic rival she had once endorsed Who is Nithya Raman, Los Angeles’s next mayor? Nithya Raman was elected to serve as the mayor of Los Angeles, defeating incumbent Karen Bass in a major
summary_zh: 曾经被认为可能性不大的洛杉矶市议员，驱逐了她曾经支持的民主党竞争对手，发生了重大改组。 谁是洛杉矶的下一届市长 Nithya Raman
body_en: Democratic socialist Nithya Raman wins Los Angeles mayoral race over incumbent Karen Bass | US midterm elections 2026
Major shake-up as LA councilmember, once considered long shot, ousts Democratic rival she had once endorsed
Who is Nithya Raman, Los Angeles’s next mayor?
Nithya Raman was elected to serve as the mayor of Los Angeles , defeating incumbent Karen Bass in a major political shake-up that reflects the growing dissatisfaction with the direction of the city.

The progressive urban planner had served on LA’s city council since 2020. She caused a stir when she entered the race earlier this year hours before the filing deadline – and shortly after endorsing Bass for re-election – and her campaign was once viewed as a long shot.
US midterm elections 2026: live results from Senate, House and governor races in all 50 states

But she shot up in the polls over the summer and, with support from the Los Angeles chapter of the Democratic Socialists of America, frequently garnered comparisons with Zohran Mamdani, New York City’s mayor.
The Associated Press called the race for Raman on Thursday, with returns showing Raman was leading with just over 52% of the votes to Bass’s 48%.

Raman’s win came after a historic election night for Democrats across the US who won control of the House and Senate in a rebuke of Donald Trump and his party. The contest in deep blue Los Angeles was unique by comparison. Raman and Bass are progressives, and the mayoral race became a bitter battle between two candidates representing different generations and frequently clashing wings of the party.
“I love this city and I love its people. And I cannot wait to get started on building a better future together with all of you,” Raman said in a video statement after her victory.
Raman also heaped praise on her former ally Bass, describing her “someone who has given decades of her life to making the city what it is today”.
The conciliatory tone marked a departure from a contentious race, where Raman and Bass traded biting remarks about each other’s perceived failures to address the city’s woes.

Bass had never before lost an election, but faced a difficult road to winning another term as mayor given her low approval ratings on par with Donald Trump’s, Angelenos’ frustration about the state of the city, and the wave of anti-establishment sentiment that has swept US politics .
The election came as Los Angeles grappled with significant challenges, including frustration over homelessness, as well as rising costs and housing affordability.
Meanwhile, the Trump administration’s deportation campaign hit the region hard, Hollywood is struggling, and the city faces a huge budget shortfall.

“While this is not the outcome we hoped for, the people of Los Angeles have spoken,” Bass said on Thursday. “I have called councilmember Nithya Raman to congratulate her on her victory, and I have committed to ensuring a smooth and seamless transition. Moving this city forward is what Los Angeles needs from all of us.”
Raman pitched herself to voters as the candidate who can “meet this moment with honesty and urgency” while lowering rents, improving city streets, reducing homelessness and keeping Angelenos safe.
She struggled in the primary – key portions of the city’s liberal base and large unions had already aligned with Bass – and was overshadowed by Spencer Pratt’s showy campaign.

Pratt, a former reality TV star and registered Republican, decided to run after he lost his home in the Palisades fire. He had splashy and viral campaign ads critical of the mayor and Raman. He was a frequent thorn in Bass’s side, arguing she was mismanaging the city, and that officials had both failed to adequately prepare for the fire and were falling short in recovery efforts.
body_zh: 民主社会主义者尼西亚·拉曼 (Nithya Raman) 击败现任凯伦·巴斯 (Karen Bass) 赢得洛杉矶市长竞选2026 年美国中期选举
曾经被认为可能性不大的洛杉矶市议员推翻了她曾经支持的民主党竞争对手，发生了重大改组
洛杉矶下一任市长 Nithya Raman 是谁？
尼西亚·拉曼（Nithya Raman）在一场重大政治变动中击败现任洛杉矶市长凯伦·巴斯（Karen Bass）当选洛杉矶市长，这反映出人们对这座城市的发展方向日益不满。
这位进步的城市规划师自 2020 年以来一直在洛杉矶市议会任职。今年早些时候，她在提交截止日期前几小时参加竞选，当时她在支持巴斯连任后不久，引起了轰动，她的竞选曾被视为希望渺茫。
2026 年美国中期选举：所有 50 个州参议院、众议院和州长竞选的实时结果
但今年夏天，她在民意调查中的支持率飙升，并且在美国民主社会主义者洛杉矶分会的支持下，经常被拿来与纽约市市长佐兰·马姆达尼进行比较。
美联社周四宣布了拉曼的竞选，结果显示拉曼以略高于 52% 的得票率领先巴斯，得票率为 48%。
拉曼的胜利是在美国各地的民主党人经历了历史性的选举之夜之后发生的，他们在唐纳德·特朗普及其政党的谴责中赢得了众议院和参议院的控制权。相比之下，在深蓝色洛杉矶举行的比赛是独一无二的。拉曼和巴斯都是进步派人士，市长竞选成为两位代表不同世代、党内两翼经常发生冲突的候选人之间的一场苦战。
“我爱这座城市，我爱它的人民。我迫不及待地想开始与你们所有人一起建设更美好的未来，”拉曼在获胜后的视频声明中说道。
拉曼还对她的前盟友巴斯大加赞扬，称她是“一个奉献了数十年生命的人，才让这座城市成为今天的样子”。
这种和解的语气标志着一场有争议的竞选的背离，当时拉曼和巴斯就彼此认为未能解决该市困境的问题交换了尖锐的言论。
巴斯以前从未输过一次选举，但由于她的支持率与唐纳德·特朗普相当，洛杉矶人对城市状况感到沮丧，以及席卷美国政坛的反建制情绪浪潮，她在连任市长时面临着一条艰难的道路。
此次选举之际，洛杉矶正在应对重大挑战，包括对无家可归者的不满，以及不断上升的成本和住房负担能力。
与此同时，特朗普政府的驱逐行动对该地区造成了沉重打击，好莱坞陷入困境，该市面临巨大的预算缺口。
“虽然这不是我们希望的结果，但洛杉矶人民已经发声了，”巴斯周四表示。 “我已致电市议员尼西亚·拉曼（Nithya Raman）祝贺她的胜利，我已承诺确保顺利、无缝的过渡。推动这座城市向前发展是洛杉矶需要我们所有人做的事情。”
拉曼向选民推销自己，称自己是一位能够“诚实而紧迫地迎接这一时刻”的候选人，同时降低租金、改善城市街道、减少无家可归者并确保洛杉矶人的安全。
她在初选中举步维艰——该市自由派基础的关键部分和大型工会已经与巴斯结盟——并被斯宾塞·普拉特华丽的竞选活动所掩盖。
普拉特是一位前真人秀明星，也是注册共和党人，他在帕利塞兹火灾中失去了家园后决定参选。他制作了引人注目且病毒式传播的竞选广告，批评市长和拉曼。他经常成为巴斯的眼中钉，认为她对这座城市的管理不善，而且官员们既没有为火灾做好充分的准备，也没有在恢复工作方面做得不够。

title_en: Gavin Newsom commutes more than 500 death sentences in California
title_zh: 加文·纽瑟姆 (Gavin Newsom) 为加州 500 多名死刑犯减刑
summary: Democrat’s move prevents these people from executions under future governors, after Christa Pike’s failed execution Gavin Newsom , California ’s governor, commuted the death sentences of more than 500 people on the state’s death row on Thursday, a move that en
summary_zh: 在克里斯塔·派克（Christa Pike）处决加利福尼亚州州长加文·纽瑟姆（Gavin Newsom）失败后，民主党的举动阻止了未来州长对这些人的处决
body_en: Gavin Newsom commutes more than 500 death sentences in California | Gavin Newsom
Democrat’s move prevents these people from executions under future governors, after Christa Pike’s failed execution

Gavin Newsom , California ’s governor, commuted the death sentences of more than 500 people on the state’s death row on Thursday, a move that ensures they can never be executed under future administrations.

The Democrat ’s mass commutation at the end of his term has converted all of the state’s death sentences to life without the possibility of parole, the largest clearing of any US death row in modern history.
The move comes after the failed execution of Christa Pike in Tennessee sparked global outrage and renewed calls for a nationwide pause on capital punishment .
His decision affects 529 men and 19 women who were sentenced to death in the state, making up the largest death row in the western hemisphere, the governor said in a letter announcing his decision.

“I take this action because I firmly believe that state-sanctioned killing is incompatible with California’s values, undermines the foundations of our legal system, and diminishes each of us,” he wrote. “I know we cannot execute people in our imperfect legal system and remain true to our core values, first among them justice and human decency.”

Newsom, considered a probable candidate for president in 2028, has long opposed the death penalty and issued a moratorium on executions in 2019. He also dismantled the state’s physical death row chamber in the infamous San Quentin prison, transferring people with death sentences to other facilities where they had more freedom of movement and access to programs – for some, a dramatic change after decades isolated in solitary cells .
Calls grow for US death penalty halt after ‘torturous’ botched execution of Christa Pike

The last execution in California was in 2006, but hundreds of people incarcerated in the state’s prisons have continued to live under death sentences, making California home to the largest death row population in the nation.

Newsom’s office noted on Thursday that of the 548 people sentenced to death, 220 of them had waited 15 years or more to be appointed habeas counsel, the legal representation they are entitled to access to fight their cases. And 139 people have waited 20 years or more for representation. If there were no moratorium in place, 45 people in the state are considered to have exhausted their appeals and would be immediately subject to execution.

“This decision is among the most difficult of my career, not because I doubt its necessity for our state but because I know its announcement may surface excruciating memories for victims’ families,” Newsom said. “I hold this painful truth along with the belief that this is a righteous action.”
The California supreme court will have to review and approve the clemency grants for cases where the individual was convicted of multiple felonies, Newsom said.

The announcement was praised by the American Civil Liberties Union and prominent advocates who oppose the death penalty, including Martin Luther King III, the eldest son of the civil rights icon, and Bryan Stevenson, an internationally renowned death penalty lawyer.

Jeanne Woodford, a former California prisons director who oversaw four executions, applauded Newsom in a statement, noting that more than 200 people nationwide had been exonerated after being sentenced to death: “As someone who has carried out executions in California, I am haunted by the fear that we will execute an innocent person.”

A relative of a victim killed by one man on California’s death row also spoke out in favor of the commutations. Jess Nichol is the sister of Polly Klaas, a 12-year-old killed in 1993 in a notorious case that paved the way for tough-on-crime laws. She said in a statement on Thursday that she used to support the execution of the man who killed her sister. “But over time I’ve realized that whether he’s executed has absolutely nothing to do with my recovery or with real public safety. The system tells survivors that execution matters to our healing. It doesn’t. It’s a distraction from what we actually need,” she said.

Governors of both parties have taken bold measures to oppose capital punishment over the years, including an Illinois Republican who commuted all 167 death sentences in 2003 before leaving office. In 2024, North Carolina’s Democratic governor, Roy Cooper, commuted 15 death sentences in the state in his final day in office.

Support for the death penalty has been declining across the US, but Democrats at times have been reluctant to do mass commutations out of fear that Republicans will paint them as “soft on crime” politicians who sided with people convicted of brutal murders.

Newsom has supported criminal justice reform efforts, including changes to prioritize rehabilitative programs in prisons . But some advocates over the years have accused him of caving to political pressures on the issue, including when he has vetoed the release of high-profile prisoners even after they have been granted parole .
body_zh: 加文·纽瑟姆 (Gavin Newsom) 在加州减刑了 500 多名死刑犯加文·纽瑟姆
在克里斯塔·派克（Christa Pike）处决失败后，民主党的举动阻止了这些人在未来州长的领导下被处决
加州州长加文·纽瑟姆 (Gavin Newsom) 周四对该州 500 多名死囚减刑，此举确保他们在未来的政府领导下永远不会被处决。
这位民主党人在任期结束时进行的大规模减刑，将该州所有死刑判决都改为无期徒刑，且不得假释，这是美国现代历史上对死囚牢房最大规模的清理。
此前，田纳西州克里斯塔·派克处决失败引发了全球的愤怒，并再次呼吁在全国范围内暂停死刑。
州长在宣布其决定的信中表示，他的决定影响了该州被判处死刑的 529 名男性和 19 名女性，这是西半球最大的死囚牢房。
他写道：“我采取这一行动是因为我坚信，国家批准的杀戮与加州的价值观不相容，破坏了我们法律体系的基础，并削弱了我们每个人的能力。” “我知道我们无法在不完善的法律体系中处决人，并忠于我们的核心价值观，首先是正义和人类尊严。”
纽瑟姆被认为是 2028 年总统的可能候选人，长期以来一直反对死刑，并于 2019 年宣布暂停执行死刑。他还拆除了臭名昭著的圣昆廷监狱的州实体死囚室，将死刑犯转移到其他设施，在那里他们有更多的行动自由和参与项目的机会 — — 对一些人来说，这是在单独牢房隔离数十年后的巨大变化。
克里斯塔·派克“惨遭”拙劣处决后，要求美国停止死刑的呼声越来越高
加州最后一次执行死刑是在 2006 年，但该州监狱中仍有数百名被判处死刑的人继续生活，这使得加州成为全美死囚人数最多的州。
纽瑟姆办公室周四指出，在 548 名被判处死刑的人中，其中 220 人等待了 15 年或更长时间才被任命为人身保护律师，这是他们有权获得的法律代表来打官司。 139 人等待代表权已达 20 年或更长时间。如果没有暂停执行，该州有 45 人将被视为已用尽上诉权，将立即被处决。
纽瑟姆说：“这个决定是我职业生涯中最困难的决定之一，不是因为我怀疑它对我们州的必要性，而是因为我知道它的宣布可能会给受害者家属带来痛苦的记忆。” “我坚持这个痛苦的事实，并相信这是一个正义的行动。”
纽瑟姆说，加州最高法院将必须审查并批准对个人被判犯有多项重罪的案件的宽大处理。
这一声明受到了美国公民自由联盟和反对死刑的知名人士的赞扬，其中包括民权偶像马丁·路德·金三世的长子和国际知名死刑律师布莱恩·史蒂文森。
负责监督四起处决的加州前监狱长珍妮·伍德福德 (Jeanne Woodford) 在一份声明中对纽瑟姆表示赞赏，并指出全国有 200 多人在被判处死刑后被无罪释放：“作为在加州执行过死刑的人，我担心我们会处决一个无辜的人。”

加州死囚牢房中被一名男子杀害的受害者的一名亲属也公开表示支持减刑。杰西·尼科尔 (Jess Nichol) 是波莉·克拉斯 (Polly Klaas) 的妹妹，波莉·克拉斯 (Polly Klaas) 12 岁，于 1993 年在一起臭名昭著的案件中被杀，这为严厉打击犯罪的法律铺平了道路。她在周四的一份声明中表示，她曾经支持处决杀害她妹妹的男子。 “但随着时间的推移，我意识到他是否被处决与我的康复或真正的公共安全完全无关。系统告诉幸存者，处决对我们的康复很重要。事实并非如此。这分散了我们真正需要的注意力，”她说。
多年来，两党州长都采取了大胆措施反对死刑，其中包括一位伊利诺伊州共和党人，他在 2003 年离任前对所有 167 名死刑犯进行了减刑。 2024 年，北卡罗来纳州民主党州长罗伊·库珀 (Roy Cooper) 在其任期的最后一天对该州 15 名死刑犯进行了减刑。
美国各地对死刑的支持率一直在下降，但民主党人有时不愿进行大规模减刑，因为担心共和党人会把他们描绘成“对犯罪软弱”的政客，站在被判犯有残酷谋杀罪的人一边。
纽瑟姆支持刑事司法改革努力，包括优先考虑监狱康复计划的改革。但多年来，一些支持者指责他在这个问题上屈服于政治压力，包括他否决释放知名囚犯，即使他们已获得假释。

title_en: US holds secret talks with Tehran to deport Iranians even as war drags on, court documents show
title_zh: 法庭文件显示，即使战争仍在继续，美国仍与德黑兰举行秘密会谈，以驱逐伊朗人
summary: Trump administration push emerges from a lawsuit alleging violations of national immigration regulations The Trump administration held secret talks with Iran on deporting Iranians even as the war there dragged on, court documents obtained by the Associated Pre
summary_zh: 特朗普政府的推动源于一项指控违反国家移民法规的诉讼 特朗普政府与特朗普政府举行了秘密会谈
body_en: Trump administration push emerges from a lawsuit alleging violations of national immigration regulations
The Trump administration held secret talks with Iran on deporting Iranians even as the war there dragged on, court documents obtained by the Associated Press show.

The court documents unsealed on Thursday show the Republican administration as recently as mid-October said it had plans to deport the Iranians through an unnamed third country, although it was unclear when it intended to do so.

The judge in the case ordered the government to give the court 24-hour notice of any finalized plans to deport Iranians to Iran or to any other country and five days’ written notice before any such deportation is carried out.

“We are at war with a country where the president of the United States has said, as recently as two or three days ago, if not yesterday, that it is essentially lawless … A country that is an enemy of the United States, according to the current president. A country that, according to our president, murdered tens of thousands of protestors,” the judge, Ana Reyes, said according to the 15 October transcript that has now been unsealed.

“And what you’re telling me is that the United States of America is going to send individuals back to that region, facing what you and I and everyone who would ever look at this would know would be, at a minimum, a serious threat of certain death.”
“Yes, your honor,” justice department attorney Dimitar Georgiev-Remmel said. “The government is executing lawful orders of removal.”

Georgiev-Remmel told the court there was no specific date set to carry out any removals. A legal group representing Iranians held by Immigration and Customs Enforcement ( ICE ) said a dozen Iranian detainees had been given notice over the past week that they would be deported to Iran. The legal group, the Iranian American Legal Defense Fund, brought the lawsuit in which the transcript was released.

The court documents show that the administration maintained contacts with Iranian officials during the war over the removals, specifically for submitting travel documents and figuring out “possible avenues for removal”.
The Department of Homeland Security (DHS), ICE’s parent agency , and the state department did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

The development emerged from an ongoing lawsuit that alleges the Trump administration’s immigration agencies have been sharing confidential information about Iranian asylum seekers with the Iranian government, violating national immigration regulations and endangering countless Iranians, court filings argue.

The Iranian American Legal Defense Fund said on Thursday at least 12 Iranian detainees have been contacted by the Iranian Interest Section, an Iranian representative office in the Pakistani embassy in Washington that handles consular affairs, in the past week and notified of an upcoming deportation flight to Iran through Pakistan. The group did not say when the deportation would occur.

One of those detainees attempted suicide once he learned he might be returned to Iran, according to Yasmine Chubin, the executive director of the organization. He was one of two people who were subsequently moved across state lines to a detention center in Texas, where detainees are often relocated immediately preceding a removal.
None of the detainees who have been contacted have been provided any information in writing from immigration authorities, the legal group said.
Activists abroad have expressed concern about deportees returning to Iran, whose theocracy has been cracking down on intellectuals and where the government vociferously cracks down on any dissent.

The lawsuit depicts a coordinated campaign between the US and Iranian governments to identify Iranians in ICE custody and pressure them to return to Iran – a marked departure from decades of diplomatic hostility between the two governments. The DHS has denied that it is sharing asylum application records with the Iranian government.

Hundreds of emails exchanged between US immigration officials exposed how the two countries worked together to arrange for more than 100 Iranians to be flown back to Iran on three immigration flights in September and December 2025 and January 2026.

During the 15 October hearing, Reyes warned government attorneys that she would initiate contempt proceedings if the administration violated her order to give the court advance notice of any planned deportation flights.
“We are talking about sending individuals in our care and custody to a country that we have bombed and we may continue bombing, and is a declared enemy of this country,” Reyes said.
body_zh: 特朗普政府的推动源于一项指控违反国家移民法规的诉讼
美联社获得的法庭文件显示，特朗普政府与伊朗就驱逐伊朗人问题进行了秘密会谈，尽管那里的战争仍在拖延。
周四公布的法庭文件显示，共和党政府最近在 10 月中旬表示，计划通过未透露姓名的第三国驱逐伊朗人，但尚不清楚其打算何时这样做。
该案法官命令政府就任何将伊朗人驱逐到伊朗或任何其他国家的最终计划提前 24 小时通知法院，并在执行任何此类驱逐之前提前五天书面通知。
根据现已启封的 10 月 15 日笔录，法官安娜·雷耶斯 (Ana Reyes) 表示：“我们正在与一个国家交战，美国总统就在两三天前甚至昨天还曾表示，这个国家本质上是无法无天的……根据现任总统的说法，这个国家是美国的敌人。根据我们的总统的说法，这个国家谋杀了数万名抗议者。”
“你告诉我的是，美利坚合众国将把一些人送回那个地区，面对你和我以及所有关注此事的人都知道，至少会面临死亡的严重威胁。”
“是的，法官大人，”司法部律师迪米塔·格奥尔基耶夫-雷梅尔说。 “政府正在执行合法的驱逐令。”
格奥尔基耶夫-雷梅尔告诉法庭，目前还没有确定具体的搬迁日期。一个代表被移民和海关执法局（ICE）关押的伊朗人的法律团体表示，过去一周已有十几名伊朗被拘留者接到通知，称他们将被驱逐到伊朗。法律团体伊朗裔美国人法律辩护基金会提起了诉讼，并公布了诉讼记录。
法庭文件显示，政府在战争期间就驱逐事宜与伊朗官员保持着联系，特别是提交旅行证件和找出“可能的驱逐途径”。
ICE 的上级机构国土安全部 (DHS) 和国务院没有立即回应置评请求。
法庭文件称，这一进展源于一项正在进行的诉讼，该诉讼指控特朗普政府的移民机构一直与伊朗政府分享有关伊朗寻求庇护者的机密信息，违反了国家移民法规，并危及无数伊朗人。
伊朗美国法律辩护基金会周四表示，过去一周，巴基斯坦驻华盛顿大使馆负责处理领事事务的伊朗代表处伊朗利益科联系了至少 12 名伊朗被拘留者，并通知他们即将通过巴基斯坦飞往伊朗。该组织没有透露何时会进行驱逐。
该组织执行主任亚斯敏·楚宾 (Yasmine Chubin) 表示，其中一名被拘留者在得知自己可能被遣返伊朗后试图自杀。他是随后被跨州转移到德克萨斯州拘留中心的两人之一，被拘留者经常在被转移之前立即被重新安置。
该法律组织表示，所联系的被拘留者均未收到移民当局的任何书面信息。
国外的活动人士对被驱逐者返回伊朗表示担忧，伊朗的神权政治一直在打压知识分子，政府也大力镇压任何异议。
该诉讼描绘了美国和伊朗政府之间协调一致的行动，以识别被 ICE 拘留的伊朗人，并迫使他们返回伊朗 — — 这明显背离了两国政府之间数十年的外交敌对状态。国土安全部否认与伊朗政府分享庇护申请记录。
美国移民官员之间交换的数百封电子邮件揭露了两国如何合作，安排100多名伊朗人在2025年9月、2025年12月和2026年1月乘坐三趟移民航班返回伊朗。
在 10 月 15 日的听证会上，雷耶斯警告政府律师，如果政府违反她向法院提前通知任何计划的驱逐航班的命令，她将启动藐视法庭诉讼。
雷耶斯说：“我们正在讨论将我们照顾和拘留的人员送往我们轰炸过的国家，我们可能会继续轰炸，并且他们是这个国家的敌人。”

The Trump administration has escalated its economic campaign against Cuba

The Trump administration on Thursday escalated its economic campaign against Cuba , issuing a determination that clears the path for U.S. sanctions on several crucial sectors of the island's economy while also targeting Chinese-based suppliers to Havana's military forces.

The sanctions are part of a larger effort by President Donald Trump and his allies to force political change in Havana even as the country continues to grapple with a deepening economic and energy crisis that has suffocated its population.
With the new penalties the State Department is expanding its reach to target new sectors of Cuba's economy, including electronics, manufacturing, marine and technology.

“Cuba’s ruling elite is hoarding the island’s energy, shipping, and technology resources for its own enrichment, leaving the Cuban people to contend with blackouts, shortages, and a stagnant economy,” Secretary of State Marco Rubio said in a statement.

In total, eight entities and two individuals were targeted, including China National Electronic Import and Export Company and Beijing H & C Technologies, two China-based companies that the U.S. is accusing of procuring weapons and selling surveillance and security equipment to the Cuban government.

Washington's campaign against Havana has only accelerated in recent months, with public spats between their representatives at the United Nations and on social media.

Last week, the U.N. General Assembly condemned the U.S. economic embargo of Cuba for the 34th year. But the U.S. campaign to influence the outcome led a number of countries to vote against the resolution or sit out the decision for the first time.

Meanwhile, Trump's threat in late January to impose tariffs on any country that sells or provides oil to Cuba has made islandwide blackouts even more common, while daily outages in Cuba now surpass 24 hours as the aging grid fails and fuel reserves dwindle.

特朗普政府周四升级了针对古巴的经济行动，发布了一项决定，为美国对该岛经济的几个关键部门实施制裁扫清了道路，同时也针对哈瓦那军队的中国供应商。
这些制裁是唐纳德·特朗普总统及其盟友为迫使哈瓦那进行政治变革而做出的更大努力的一部分，尽管该国仍在努力应对日益严重的经济和能源危机，该危机已导致其民众窒息。
通过新的处罚措施，国务院正在扩大制裁范围，瞄准古巴经济的新领域，包括电子、制造、海洋和技术。
美国国务卿马可·卢比奥在一份声明中表示：“古巴的统治精英正在囤积岛上的能源、航运和技术资源，以谋取私利，使古巴人民面临停电、短缺和经济停滞的困境。”
总共有八个实体和两名个人成为攻击目标，其中包括中国电子进出口公司和北京宏创科技有限公司，美国指控这两家中国公司向古巴政府采购武器并向古巴政府出售监控和安全设备。

上周，联合国大会谴责美国对古巴实施的第34年经济封锁。但美国影响结果的行动导致一些国家首次投票反对该决议或袖手旁观。

body_en: The judge oversaw extradition proceedings in Mexico for a Canadian citizen allegedly helping Ryan Wedding
A Mexican judge has been arrested and accused of accepting $2m in bribes in exchange for releasing a suspected Canadian drug trafficker from custody, US officials said on Thursday.

Luis Benítez Alcántara was overseeing extradition proceedings in Mexico in 2024 for Canadian citizen Andrew Clark, who was charged in the US with helping to run a billion-dollar drug-trafficking group allegedly headed by the former Canadian Olympic snowboarder Ryan Wedding, the justice department said in a statement.
Ryan Wedding’s journey from Olympic snowboarder to alleged cocaine kingpin
Benítez is accused of releasing Clark from custody after accepting the bribe payments, according to the statement.
Clark was arrested days after his release and removed to the United States, where he faces drug-trafficking and murder charges.
The statement said Benítez, 49, was arrested on Sunday in Colombia. He is charged in a nine count indictment with being an accessory after the fact. It was not immediately known if he has a lawyer.
US officials will request Benítez’s extradition from Colombia, the statement said.

“Crooked public officials, no matter where they are, who assist drug traffickers operating here at home will face justice in the United States,” the US attorney general, Todd Blanche, said in the statement.

It is the latest arrest in the US investigation into a multinational drug-trafficking network allegedly run by Wedding, who became a top FBI fugitive accused of moving cocaine from Latin America into the United States and orchestrating several killings. Wedding was arrested in Mexico earlier this year and flown to California, where he pleaded not guilty to murder and drug charges.

Dozens of people have been arrested in connection with the alleged drug network, and authorities seized large volumes of drugs, weapons and cash, as well as millions of dollars’ worth of automobiles, motorcycles, artwork and jewelry in its investigation.
Clark’s attorney, Matthew Lombard, did not immediately respond to messages on Thursday.
body_zh: 法官在墨西哥监督了一名涉嫌帮助瑞安婚礼的加拿大公民的引渡程序
美国官员周四表示，一名墨西哥法官已被捕，并被指控收受 200 万美元贿赂，以换取释放一名加拿大毒贩嫌疑人。
司法部在一份声明中称，路易斯·贝尼特斯·阿尔坎塔拉正在墨西哥监督 2024 年加拿大公民安德鲁·克拉克 (Andrew Clark) 的引渡程序，后者在美国被指控帮助运营一个价值数十亿美元的贩毒集团，据称该集团由前加拿大单板滑雪运动员瑞安·威丁 (Ryan Wedding) 领导。
瑞安·威丁 (Ryan Wedding) 从奥林匹克滑雪运动员到涉嫌可卡因头目的历程
声明称，贝尼特斯被指控在收受贿赂后将克拉克释放。
克拉克在获释几天后被捕，并被送往美国，在那里他面临贩毒和谋杀指控。
声明称，49 岁的贝尼特斯周日在哥伦比亚被捕。他被指控为事后从犯的九项罪名。目前尚不清楚他是否有律师。
声明称，美国官员将要求哥伦比亚引渡贝尼特斯。
美国司法部长托德·布兰奇在声明中表示：“在国内协助毒贩的不诚实的公职人员，无论身在何处，都将在美国面临正义。”
这是美国对据称由威丁经营的跨国贩毒网络进行的调查中最新逮捕的一起，威丁成为联邦调查局的一名头号逃犯，被指控将可卡因从拉丁美洲运送到美国并策划了多起杀戮。维丁今年早些时候在墨西哥被捕，并飞往加利福尼亚州，在那里他对谋杀和毒品指控不认罪。
数十人因涉嫌毒品网络而被捕，当局在调查中查获了大量毒品、武器和现金，以及价值数百万美元的汽车、摩托车、艺术品和珠宝。
克拉克的律师马修·隆巴德周四没有立即回复消息。

title_en: Who is Nithya Raman, the democratic socialist who will be Los Angeles’s next mayor?
